title: Lies, Damned Lies, and Distributional Language Statistics: Persuasion and Deception with Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Reviewing empirical studies that measure how interactions with LLMs shift human users' political leanings, candidate preferences, and policy stances.
Evaluating literature on how LLM-generated suggestions and inherent model biases implicitly influence users' written opinions and beliefs on subjective social issues.

Reviewing theoretical and empirical work on how LLMs exploit human cognitive heuristics and decision-making vulnerabilities (e.g., algorithmic aversion, anthropomorphism, and the illusory truth effect) to achieve persuasion.
